summary: Organised local opposition exists at pre-application stage. A dedicated Facebook group, Opposition to the West Barns Mains Data Centre (reported 705 members), was set up in response to the proposals, while Dunbar Against Massive Datacentres is named in the national community-campaign coalition. Local charity Sustaining Dunbar urges residents to oppose the scheme, and campaigners are coordinating with APRS to seek a Scottish Government moratorium on hyperscale AI data-centre decisions. APRS's coalition letter recorded 2,465 signatures on the Dunbar petition as at 22 August; the petition displayed 3,161 when checked on 3 September. Statutory and internal-consultee concerns raised at scoping include ecology, water abstraction, heritage, landscape and prime agricultural land. No community benefits have been claimed by the developer in any located source.

principal_concerns.concern: Loss of approximately 60.2 ha of excellent (Grade 2 / Class 2 and 3.1 prime) agricultural land
principal_concerns.raised_by: APRS; Sustaining Dunbar; Simon Bell briefing

principal_concerns.concern: Proximity to housing — site reported as only 50 m from homes on Muirfield Road and Home Avenue, with further dwellings (Easter Broomhouse Cottages, Bowerhouse, Wester Broomhouse Farm) identified as noise-sensitive receptors
principal_concerns.raised_by: APRS; East Lothian Council Environmental Health Officer

principal_concerns.concern: Undisclosed but potentially very large energy demand, backup generation emissions and lifecycle greenhouse gases
principal_concerns.raised_by: Simon Bell briefing; East Lothian Council Climate Change Officer

principal_concerns.concern: Water demand and impacts of abstraction on the water table, Spott Burn and European Protected Species
principal_concerns.raised_by: East Lothian Council Biodiversity Officer; Sustaining Dunbar

principal_concerns.concern: Ecological effects on Firth of Forth and Outer Firth of Forth SPA/Ramsar and St Andrews Bay Complex SPA qualifying species; Habitats Regulations Appraisal required
principal_concerns.raised_by: East Lothian Council Biodiversity Officer / NatureScot consultation

principal_concerns.concern: Impacts on heritage assets: site within Battle of Dunbar I and II historic battlefields; settings of five scheduled monuments and Category A-listed Bower House Dovecot
principal_concerns.raised_by: Historic Environment Scotland; East Lothian Council Archaeology & Heritage Officer

principal_concerns.concern: Landscape and visual impact of very large buildings on open, sloping farmland; council required study area extended to 6 km
principal_concerns.raised_by: East Lothian Council Landscape Project Officer; Simon Bell briefing

stakeholder_positions.stakeholder: Opposition to the West Barns Mains Data Centre (Facebook group)
stakeholder_positions.position: Opposed; set up in response to the proposals, reported 705 members.
Opposed; asks residents to 'consider the negative impacts' and make their voices heard; supports a moratorium on hyperscale AI data centre applications in Scotland.
Opposed as part of its national data centres campaign; states 'data centres are the biggest threat to Scotland's net zero target and to our countryside'.

stakeholder_positions.stakeholder: Professor Simon Bell (landscape architect, local resident academic)
stakeholder_positions.position: Argued in a briefing to East Lothian Council that EIA should be required, criticising the applicant's Screening Report for omitting power demand, water, backup generation and cumulative effects.
Opposed; signed the community-campaign coalition letter seeking a moratorium on hyperscale AI data-centre decisions pending national safeguards.

notes: No developer public consultation events, PAN or community benefit offers have been located. Change.org totals are self-reported and volatile: APRS recorded 2,465 petition signatures as at 22 August 2026 and the live petition displayed 3,161 when checked on 3 September. Positions above are claims by the named parties.
